body_text:
The integer represented by a pair $(a,b)$ of natural numbers is
the formal difference $a-b$. The equivalence relation
$(a,b)\sim(c,d)$ is defined by $a+d=b+c$, avoiding subtraction
in $\mathbb{N}$. Addition and multiplication on equivalence
classes are legitimate only after proving that their values do
not depend on the chosen representatives.
